summary: Hydrate posts and members into the local SQLite mirror, add posts list / members list, and surface per-resource sync failures in agent mode.
reason: defaultSyncResources() returned only ["notifications"] and syncResourcePath() knew only /notifications, so sync hydrated one resource and the SQLite mirror, FTS search, and cross-community SQL (this CLI's headline differentiators) had nothing to read. The cause is upstream of sync: the spec declared no plain list endpoint for posts or members, because both are rendered inside the community page's Next.js pageProps envelope, which the generated flat-list loop cannot unwrap. `sync --resources posts,members` therefore failed with `unknown sync resource`, and that error was returned without ever being printed in agent mode, leaving only the aggregate `N resource(s) failed to sync`.
validated_outcome: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` clean; `cli-printing-press publish validate` passes. `posts list` and `members list` register and expose --community/--pages/--limit. Per-resource failures emit exactly one sync_error event in agent mode: the aggregation loop in sync.go is the sole emission point, and every worker-level failure path sets Err and stays silent, so an agent counting failures sees one line per failed resource. The wrapped worker errors (e.g. "fetching posts page 2: ...") are what the aggregation prints, so consolidating lost no detail. sync_warning paths return Warn rather than Err and are unaffected. TestSyncSkoolCommunityResourceDoesNotEmitSyncError pins the contract.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Spec-declared items path for enveloped list endpoints
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The list endpoints added to spec.yaml carry an x-items-path hint the generator does not yet read, so sync_skool.go hand-writes the unwrap. Once the generator honors a per-endpoint items path, this file should collapse back into the generated sync loop.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Non-cursor pagination in the generated sync loop
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Skool paginates the community page with an integer `p` param, not limit/cursor. The generated loop only knows limit/cursor pairs.
